episode.tagline: Welcome to Episode 2 of Everything is Everything, a weekly podcast hosted by Amit Varma and Ajay Shah. New episodes release every Friday. Please like and subscribe!
episode.about: In this episode, Amit and Ajay talk about artificial intelligence. How will it change the world? How excited should we be? How scared should we be? Also discussed: pioneering feminists, pioneering monsters and pioneering masala chai.

items.content: Told by the producer to drop his 'resting pout face', Amit promises a 'jokerish permanent smile' for the rest of the episode. Then Ajay:…
Amit: 'we of course are artists as we discussed in the last episode. That was an allegation made on us.'
Ajay imagines an LLM reading everything the two hosts have written, guessing 'that we are nutcases', and arriving at the name Everything…
Amit on protein folding: 'if you've ever seen me wrap a piece of bacon around a sausage, you'll realize I'm bloody good at protein…
Amit on Mary Wollstonecraft: 'Married to an interesting guy, also a bit of an asshole, but leave him out of the equation.'
Amit closes the AI debate: they 'agree to disagree genially, as AI also would, because no emotions — we are the messed up creatures.'
Ajay's wife Susan says his herbal 'tea' isn't tea at all, because there's no tea in it.
The 'third host' is Mark, who cavorted in the background and fell asleep on a bookshelf. The producers said they hadn't heard a word the…
Hemingway, quoted by Ajay on the craft of writing: 'a good day is one in which you write one good sentence.'
Ken Thompson's dynamic-programming algorithm for chess endgames. Ajay: it was 'like a thunderbolt going off' when it arrived and is…
Idealism vs materialism: Ajay puts himself 'on the materialism side. There is nothing happening in the skull other than some quantum…
Amit invokes the old idea that enough monkeys will eventually type Shakespeare, as a way to think about AI matching great creative work.
Ajay's architecture analogy: a model standing at Akbar's tomb in Sikandra would never invent the Taj Mahal, the next step in 'the great…
Amit, deflating human exceptionalism: 'some would of course argue we are colonized by bacteria, we're colonized by wheat.'
Ajay: if you grant conscious AGI, 'then we're building von Neumann machines. We're colonizing the galaxy.'
Ajay on AI regulation: 'I want to be fully Coasean. You don't have to have governments doing all the heavy lifting.'
